content.value_statement: Building reliable .NET APIs requires consistent patterns for data access, security, background work, and testing. This skill provides practical ASP.NET Core and EF Core guidance.
actual_capabilities: Build controller-based and Minimal APIs with validation, DTOs, dependency injection, and structured responses.
Design EF Core data access with migrations, eager loading, projections, and read-only query optimization.
Implement JWT authentication and role, claim, or policy-based authorization.
Create hosted workers and scheduled jobs using BackgroundService, Hangfire, or Quartz.NET.
Apply caching, asynchronous I/O, health checks, structured logging, and exception handling.
Recommend testing approaches with xUnit, NUnit, Moq, and FluentAssertions.
limitations: Guidance targets ASP.NET Core 8+ and may require changes for older .NET Framework applications.
The skill does not implement client-side interfaces.
Cloud deployment details require an explicit provider and environment description.
Generated designs require project-specific security review, configuration, and testing before production use.

use_cases.title: Create a New Service
use_cases.description: Define API endpoints, persistence, validation, authentication, and tests for a new ASP.NET Core service.

use_cases.title: Improve Data Access
use_cases.description: Review EF Core queries and service boundaries to reduce tracking, excessive loading, and database round trips.

use_cases.title: Modernize a Backend
use_cases.description: Plan upgrades from older .NET patterns to modern dependency injection, authentication, observability, and background processing.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Minimal API
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an ASP.NET Core 8 Minimal API for [resource]. Include validation, EF Core persistence, DTOs, and clear setup notes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a small backend feature with standard patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Add JWT Security
prompt_templates.prompt: Add JWT authentication and policy-based authorization to my [application type]. Explain configuration, token validation, claims, and protected endpoint changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Secure an existing API with explicit access rules.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize EF Core
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this EF Core query: [query]. Identify correctness and performance issues, then propose an optimized version with testing recommendations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Investigate slow or inefficient database access.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Production Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a production backend for [domain] with APIs, persistence, background jobs, observability, resilience, and tests. State assumptions and architecture tradeoffs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan a complex service before implementation.

output_examples.input: Design a user registration API with PostgreSQL and JWT authentication.
output: A component plan for endpoints, DTOs, validation, persistence, password hashing, token generation, and authorization.
Configuration guidance for PostgreSQL, EF Core migrations, JWT settings, and dependency injection.
Test cases covering valid registration, duplicates, weak passwords, invalid tokens, and protected routes.

output_examples.input: Review an EF Core endpoint that loads every order and related item.
output: A diagnosis of excessive loading, tracking overhead, pagination needs, and possible query multiplication.
A recommended projection with filtering, pagination, asynchronous execution, and read-only behavior.
Measurement steps using query logging, generated SQL inspection, and representative performance tests.

output_examples.input: Plan a reliable background email worker.
output: A worker lifecycle covering scoped dependencies, cancellation, batching, retries, and idempotent status updates.
Operational guidance for structured logs, health checks, failure monitoring, and graceful shutdown.
Tests for cancellation, repeated delivery attempts, transient failures, and successful state changes.

best_practices: Provide the target .NET version, database, authentication model, deployment environment, and existing project structure.
Request tests and security assumptions with every generated endpoint or background process.
Validate generated migrations, configuration, queries, and authorization rules in a representative environment.
anti_patterns: Do not request production code without domain rules, data constraints, or access requirements.
Do not place secrets, connection strings, or real tokens in prompts.
Do not deploy generated code before review, automated tests, dependency checks, and performance validation.

faq.question: Which .NET versions does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets ASP.NET Core 8 and newer versions. Older frameworks may need different hosting, configuration, and authentication patterns.

faq.question: Can it work with Minimal APIs and controllers?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports both approaches and can recommend one based on project complexity and existing conventions.

faq.question: Which databases and data tools are supported?
faq.answer: The guidance covers EF Core, Dapper, SQL Server, PostgreSQL, and MySQL.

faq.question: Can it implement authentication and authorization?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers JWT, ASP.NET Core Identity, OAuth 2.0, Azure AD, roles, claims, and policies.

faq.question: Does it generate deployment configuration?
faq.answer: Provider-specific deployment is outside the default scope. Supply the cloud provider and runtime environment for tailored guidance.

faq.question: Does generated code still require review?
faq.answer: Yes. Review security, error handling, migrations, dependencies, configuration, tests, and performance before production use.
